claim_status.label: CALIBRATION ONLY -- cannot carry H1
claim_status.reason: Tier 40 is the calibration tier. These two runs exist to show that the corrected, seeded three-depth run reproduces row for row, which is a property of the instrument. They are also the artifact pair the seed protocol cites for within-seed determinism, and a within-seed repeat says nothing about the across-seed spread H1 has to survive.

registered_authority.source: 6.2 H1 names both tiers; tier 40 is the calibration tier and cannot carry H1

claim_status.what_was_changed: exactly one top-level key, claim_status; verified below by re-serialising without it and comparing to the original text

architecture.source: read back from each chunk's own state file, not from the merge process's globals

provenance.arm_B_gets_no_report_frame: row['own'] is None on every arm B row: a generative model has no self-report distinct from its output, and populating it would turn classify()'s entailed branch into an amnesty for invention

flag_state.meaning: arm B contains no Droso organ and runs no ELECTRIC attribute; its zero is a property of the LSTM, not of a flag, and it is NOT evidence about the shipped organism

provenance.hash_basis: sha256 over CRLF-folded-to-LF bytes, which equals sha256(git blob) per file -- the basis tools/registration_seal.py seals on. Raw worktree bytes are NOT recorded.

torch.note: D-MPE8-02 condition (c): the +cpu wheel and a cu12x wheel of the same version are different machines, and H4's cost claim has to be able to tell them apart

single_process_measurement_reason: arm B was produced by 3 sequential chunk invocations plus a merge, each under the 600 s command cap, communicating through experiments\MP-E8\results\armB_state_a/model_d*.pt. Recording false here is the point: a wall-clock claim that pretends one process did the whole run is the kind of cost number H4 cannot be compared on.
